## P1 Blocker

### UX-039 — Link a "Report claim" task to its claim, and stop offering a second claim
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager or CSR, within 24 hours of a loss, working a claim task ranked "New claim".
- **Where:**
  - `web/src/app/(app)/claims/actions.ts:27-28` creates a `CLAIM-FNOL` task with `claimId` set, subject "Report claim CLM-… to the carrier".
  - `web/src/app/(app)/tasks/[id]/page.tsx:61` shows "Record claim →" for every `CLAIM-FNOL` task and doesn't check `claim_id`. Only `CLAIM-FU` gets "Open claim" (`:67`).
  - `claims/actions.ts:39-47`: ticking "Reported to carrier" saves but leaves the task open.
- **What the user experiences:** The task says to report CLM-26-0142. Its only primary button opens a blank "Record claim" form, and nothing on the screen links to CLM-26-0142. Saving that form creates a second claim, closes the task as "Claim recorded", and opens another "Report claim" task. If they instead find the claim through the client page and tick "Reported to carrier", the flash says "Saved" and the task stays in the queue.
- **Why it matters:** The screen steers the user to a duplicate claim while the 24-hour reporting clock runs. A correct report also leaves stale urgent work behind, which weakens trust in the queue.
- **Recommendation:**
  - In `tasks/[id]/page.tsx:61`, show "Record claim" only when `claim_id` is null. When it is set, show "Open claim CLM-26-0142 →".
  - On the claim page, show the banner "Not reported to the carrier yet" with one action, "Mark reported", beside the carrier claim number.
  - When a claim becomes reported, close its open `CLAIM-FNOL` task and flash "Marked reported. The task is closed. Next task →".
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Report claim CLM-26-0142 to the carrier
          [New claim] [Due today]
          [Record claim →]                 → blank new-claim form  ◀
  AFTER   Report claim CLM-26-0142 to the carrier
          [New claim] [Due today]
          [Open claim CLM-26-0142 →]                               ◀
          Claim page: [Mark reported] → task closes · Next task →  ◀
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-039.html`
- **Verify:** Record a claim without "Already reported". The task's button opens that claim, and marking it reported closes the task. No path from that task can create a second claim.

## P2 Major

### UX-006 — Make "Done & next" reversible and say what was done
- **Status:** Improved (first seen 2026-11-01). The queue's "✓ Done" now shows a pending state, names the task and offers Undo, and finished tasks have Reopen. Still missing: "Done & next" and completing with a follow-up.
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager moving through focus mode.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/tasks/actions.ts:43-44`; `tasks/next/route.ts` forwards `msg` only.
- **What the user experiences:** After "Done & next →", the bar reads "Done. Here's your next task." It doesn't name the finished task or offer a way back. This is the fastest path in the app, and the only safety net is finding the old task again.
- **Why it matters:** A slip in focus mode costs more than a slip in the queue, because the finished task is already off screen.
- **Recommendation:** Pass `undo={id}` through `/tasks/next`, so `TaskFlash` shows `Completed "Issue certificate for Bluefin Analytics". Undo`. Add Undo to the "Done — follow-up set for Nov 7" message too, and cancel the follow-up when Undo is used.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  ┌ Done. Here's your next task. ──────────────────┐
  AFTER   ┌ Completed "Issue certificate for Bluefin        ◀
          │  Analytics".                          [Undo]    ◀
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-006.html` (from an earlier run, still accurate)
- **Verify:** Click "Done & next", then Undo on the next task's page, and the first task returns at the same rank.

- **Why it matters:** These are the two forms where retyping invites a money or date error.
- **Recommendation:** Move both to the existing `useActionState` and `rejected()` pattern used by `EndorseForm`.
- **Before / after:**

  ```
  AFTER   ✖ That period is locked.
          Amount [2500.00]  Check # [10442]  Memo [Oct renewal]  ◀
  ```

- **Verify:** Post a receipt dated in a locked month. The typed values remain.

### UX-037 — Load the client's details the moment it is picked
- **Status:** Improved (first seen 2026-11-02). The form can no longer save a client other than the one shown; it blocks and explains. That creates a new interruption, though.

Press the Load button by the client box first." The amber note warns that loading "clears anything you typed below". So they must load, then retype.

  Mockup: `UX-037.html` (previous run, direction still right)
- **Verify:** Pick a client and create a task with no extra click. Nothing typed is lost.

### UX-040 — Start a reissue from the old certificate, and stop pre-ticking Additional insured
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** CSR changing a certificate while a client waits on the phone.
- **Where:**
  - `web/src/app/(app)/certificates/[id]/page.tsx:44`: "Reissue with changes" passes only `client` and `holder`.
  - `web/src/app/(app)/certificates/new/page.tsx:42-43`: without a task, `ai` is on, `wos` and `pnc` are off, and policies reset to every liability line.
  - `lib/certificates.ts:109`: issuing supersedes the holder's previous certificate.
- **What the user experiences:** A certificate has Additional insured, Waiver and Primary & non-contributory on two policies. "Reissue with changes" opens with only Additional insured ticked and all liability policies ticked. To change one address, the CSR must notice what vanished. A holder who never asked for it also gets the printed additional insured wording by default on any certificate started outside a task.
- **Why it matters:** The new certificate replaces the old one, so a dropped waiver reaches a contractor as a coverage statement they can't use. A pre-ticked additional insured line promises something nobody requested.
- **Recommendation:**
  - Add `from={id}` to the link, and load wording, policies and description from that certificate. Show "Starting from COI-26-01190. Change what differs."
  - For a new certificate with a previous one on file for this holder, use its flags. Otherwise default all three boxes off.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  (old cert: AI, Waiver, P&NC · GL, Umbrella)
          [x] Additional insured  [ ] Waiver  [ ] Primary & NC   ◀
          [x] GL  [x] Auto  [x] WC  [x] Umbrella                 ◀
  AFTER   Starting from COI-26-01190. Change what differs.       ◀
          [x] Additional insured  [x] Waiver  [x] Primary & NC   ◀
          [x] GL  [ ] Auto  [ ] WC  [x] Umbrella                 ◀
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-040.html`
- **Verify:** Reissue a certificate with all three flags. The form opens matching it, and a certificate started fresh from a client page has none ticked.

### UX-041 — Update the email and description when the holder changes
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** CSR issuing to a holder other than the one picked from the request.
- **Where:**
  - `web/src/app/(app)/certificates/new/page.tsx:41` computes `email` and `description` once, for the preselected holder.
  - `certificates/new/holder-choice.tsx:20`: changing the select updates only the "replaces" note.
  - `certificates/new/issue-form.tsx:41` and `holder-choice.tsx:30` both offer a holder email field.
- **What the user experiences:** With Hendrick Brothers preselected, the CSR picks Crescent Realty instead. "Email to" still holds Hendrick's address, and the description still describes Hendrick's job. With email connected, Crescent's certificate goes to Hendrick. With a new holder and email off, two fields are labelled "Holder email…" on one form.
- **Why it matters:** A certificate reaches the wrong third party, or goes out describing the wrong job.
- **Recommendation:** Pass each holder's email and last description to the client form, and on change replace them when the user hasn't edited them. If they have, show "Use Crescent's: leasing@crescent.com". Make new-holder mode feed one Delivery email field and remove the duplicate.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Holder [Crescent Realty Partners ▾]
          Description [Glenwood Ave tenant upfit…]   (Hendrick's)  ◀
          Email to    [pm@hendrickbros.com]          (Hendrick's)  ◀
  AFTER   Holder [Crescent Realty Partners ▾]
          Description [Lot 14 lease, all operations]               ◀
          Email to    [leasing@crescentrealty.com]                 ◀
  ```
  Mockup: inline only
- **Verify:** Change the holder. Email and description follow unless already edited.

### UX-042 — Say what's blocking the action when a task has no policy or client
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager on an emailed request that named no policy, such as "we bought a new car".
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/tasks/[id]/page.tsx:56-66`. The endorse, cancel, non-pay, ID card and dec page shortcuts need `t.policy_id`, and all shortcuts need `t.client_id`. The "Linked policy" card sits low in the right column (`:238`).
- **What the user experiences:** The task reads "Endorsement request" with no button at all. Nothing says the button appears once a policy is linked. On a non-pay task, the most urgent type, the "Resolve non-pay" panel is simply absent.
- **Why it matters:** The user must guess why the next step is missing. That breaks "what do I do next" on a common kind of email.
- **Recommendation:** When a shortcut is held back, show its place in "What's needed": "Pick the policy to endorse:" with the client's in-force policies as an inline select that saves and reveals "Endorse policy →". With no client, show "Link a client first", leading to the existing picker.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  What's needed
          We bought a 2026 RAV4, please add it.
          (no buttons)                                        ◀
  AFTER   What's needed
          We bought a 2026 RAV4, please add it.
          Which policy should this endorse?                   ◀
          [BEA-1123 · Personal auto ▾] [Endorse policy →]     ◀
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-042.html`
- **Verify:** Open an END-REQ task with no policy, pick one in place, and land on the endorse form with the task attached.

### UX-043 — Reply to the email from the task
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** M
- **Who / when:** Account manager answering a billing or service question, which is the most common email task.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/tasks/[id]/page.tsx:98` offers only "Open in inbox"; the Reply card is at `inbox/[id]/page.tsx:51-57`; `inbox/actions.ts:105` returns to the email.
- **What the user experiences:** To answer a question they just read, the user leaves focus mode, replies on the email page, clicks the Task link in the side panel to go back, and then clicks "Done & next".
- **Why it matters:** The product's promise is finishing work on one screen, and replying is the action most tasks need.
- **Recommendation:** Add a Reply box under the original email in the focus view, posting to `replyAction` with a return path to the task. After sending, flash "Reply sent to …" with the Finish panel still on screen, and prefill Outcome with "Replied to client". Offer "Send & wait on client" as a second button.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Original email                     [Open in inbox]
          Can you tell me what's still owed on Brown Electric?
  AFTER   Original email                     [Open in inbox]
          Can you tell me what's still owed on Brown Electric?
          Reply to pm@brownelectric.com                     ◀
          [                                  ]              ◀
          [Send reply] [Send & wait on client]              ◀
  ```
  Mockup: inline only
- **Verify:** Answer an email and finish its task without leaving the task page.

### UX-044 — Keep coverage-risk work from leaving the queue past its deadline
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** M
- **Who / when:** Account manager clearing "Do now" between interruptions.
- **Where:**
  - `web/src/components/tasks.tsx:41,48`: "✓ Done" and "⏱ Later → Next week" appear on every row.
  - `lib/priority.ts:101`: a snoozed task stays out of the queue until its date.
  - `lib/work.ts:215-226`: the daily non-pay reminder raises priority but leaves the snooze in place.
  - `lib/automation.ts:33-34`: a closed automated non-pay task can't be recreated, because its key already exists.
  - `lib/automation.ts:94`: the policy then cancels by itself on its date.
- **What the user experiences:** On "cancels Nov 4 unless paid", dated Nov 3, "Next week" is one click away. The task leaves the queue until after the cancellation, with no warning. "✓ Done" on the same row closes it with no outcome, and no new task appears.
- **Why it matters:** Coverage can lapse with nobody looking, on the exact items the queue ranks highest.
- **Recommendation:**
  - For `NONPAY`, `UW-CANC`, `BINDER-EXP` and renewals within 7 days, replace the quick "✓ Done" with "Resolve →", which opens the focus view.
  - Grey out any snooze or wait option past the deadline, marked "Cancels Nov 4", and offer "Until Nov 3" instead.
  - In the daily check, clear a snooze when the deadline is 2 days away or less, and note "Back in your queue: cancels Nov 4".
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Piedmont Haulers … cancels 2026-11-04   [✓ Done] [⏱ Later]
          Snooze until: [Tomorrow] [3 days] [Next week]
  AFTER   Piedmont Haulers … cancels Nov 4        [Resolve →] [⏱ Later] ◀
          Snooze until: [Tomorrow]  3 days · Next week: after Nov 4    ◀
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-044.html`
- **Verify:** A non-pay task can't be snoozed past its cancel date. A snoozed one returns 2 days before it.

### UX-045 — Leave the renewal premium blank and show the change before saving
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** M
- **Who / when:** Account manager entering a renewal offer.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/policies/[id]/page.tsx:303` defaults the premium to expiring; `:299` guesses the next policy number; the comparison and "Over remarket threshold" appear only on the new term (`:348`).
- **What the user experiences:** The form opens with Renewal premium already filled at the expiring figure and a policy number ending one higher. Clicking "Create renewal term" without changing them records a 0.0% renewal. If the real number is 18% higher, the user learns it crossed the remarket threshold only after the term exists.
- **Why it matters:** A pre-filled number looks verified, as on the receipt form fixed under UX-029. The remarket decision should come before the term is created, since it is an E&O record.
- **Recommendation:**
  - Leave Renewal premium blank, labelled "Renewal premium (from the carrier's offer)", with the hint "Expiring $4,684".
  - As the user types, show "+$843 (+18.0%). Over the 10% remarket threshold" with a link "Mark as remarketing".
  - Keep the suggested policy number but say "Suggested. Check against the carrier's renewal."
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Renewal premium (expiring $4,684) [4684.00]              ◀
          [Create renewal term]
  AFTER   Renewal premium [ 5527.00 ]  Expiring $4,684             ◀
          +$843 (+18.0%). Over the 10% remarket threshold          ◀
          [Mark as remarketing]  [Create renewal term]             ◀
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-045.html`
- **Verify:** The form can't be submitted without a typed premium, and the percentage appears before saving.

### UX-046 — Show the items behind a carrier payment
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** M
- **Who / when:** Accounting manager paying a carrier by statement from trust.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/accounting/payables/page.tsx:29-35` shows payee, item count, oldest date and total. "Paid statements" shows totals only, and neither table has a drill-down.
- **What the user experiences:** The row reads "Granite Ridge Mutual · 12 · $12,480.15 · [Pay statement]". The dialog correctly names the amount, but the user can't see which 12 items make it up before paying, or afterwards when a carrier asks what the payment covered. The flash reads "Carrier statement paid from trust", without the amount or reference.
- **Why it matters:** This user needs certainty before moving fiduciary money, and carriers reconcile by item.
- **Recommendation:** Expand each row to show invoice, client, policy, gross, commission and net, with a total matching the row. Do the same for paid statements, plus "Download remittance (CSV)". Flash "Paid Granite Ridge Mutual $12,480.15, ref ACH 1104 (12 items)."
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Granite Ridge Mutual  12  2026-09-02  $12,480.15 [Pay statement]
  AFTER   ▾ Granite Ridge Mutual  12  Sep 2  $12,480.15  [Pay statement] ◀
            INV-26-0412 Brown Electric  GRM-5512  $2,100.00              ◀
            INV-26-0433 Cary Dental     GRM-7781    $884.20  …           ◀
            Total 12 items                        $12,480.15             ◀
  ```
  Mockup: `UX-046.html`
- **Verify:** The listed items add up to the amount in the confirmation, and a paid statement can be reopened to see them.

- **Status:** New

  - Add opportunities to search.

  Mockup: inline only

- **Where:**
  - `ClientPicker` still announces "Client" for "Insured", "Client with an open balance" and "Client or prospect" unless `label` is passed: `certificates/new/page.tsx:16`, `claims/new/page.tsx:16`, `accounting/receipts/new/page.tsx:34`.
  - Placeholder-only fields: Tasks filters (`tasks/page.tsx:67-71`), coverage rows (`policy-form.tsx:45`), submission update (`sales/[id]/page.tsx:51-54`), renewal stage (`policies/[id]/page.tsx:318-319`), statement resolve (`commissions/[id]/page.tsx:58-59`).
  - `text-slate-400` on information: statement line notes (`commissions/[id]/page.tsx:51`), invoice memos (`clients/[id]/page.tsx:378`), who issued a certificate (`certificates/page.tsx:43`), who recorded a transaction (`policies/[id]/page.tsx:148`).
  - The header search removes its outline and shows only a border change (`global-search.tsx:10`).
- **What the user experiences:** Filters are announced with no purpose, and the reason on a commission line is the faintest text on the row.
- **Why it matters:** These are small gaps on screens used all day.
- **Recommendation:** Pass `label` on those pickers, add `aria-label` to the listed fields, change these uses to `text-slate-500`, and add `focus:ring-2 focus:ring-indigo-100` to the search box.
- **Verify:** A screen-reader pass names every filter, and these texts pass AA contrast.

### UX-048 — Offer a way back from Ignored, Cancelled and Lost
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager who ignored an email by mistake; producer whose lost deal revives.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/inbox/[id]/page.tsx:91`, `tasks/[id]/page.tsx:94` (Reopen only for `done`), `sales/[id]/page.tsx:73` (stage card hidden once closed).
- **What the user experiences:** An ignored email has no Restore, and its cancelled task has no Reopen. A lost opportunity has no controls, even though `resumeWith` already supports reopening a cancelled task.
- **Why it matters:** Client requests shouldn't become unrecoverable after one misjudged click.
- **Recommendation:** Add "Restore to triage" on ignored email (reopens the task), "Reopen" on cancelled tasks, and "Reopen opportunity" on lost ones.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Status: ignored     (no actions)
  AFTER   Status: ignored     [Restore to triage]   ◀
  ```
  Mockup: inline only
- **Verify:** Ignore an email, restore it, and it returns to triage with an open task.

### UX-049 — Enforce the reason the form calls required, and confirm Lost
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager recording a remarket or lost decision.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/policies/[id]/page.tsx:319` says "Reason (required for remarket, lost, non-renewal)". `lib/policies.ts:228` and `policies/actions.ts:169-185` accept a blank reason, with no confirmation. `sales/actions.ts:30` stores "Not specified".
- **What the user experiences:** Choosing Lost with an empty reason succeeds. All renewal tasks close, and the flash reads only "Renewal stage updated", without mentioning the closed tasks or the new remarket task.
- **Why it matters:** The remarket decision is an E&O record, and the lost-business report shows "—" for the reason.
- **Recommendation:** Reject a blank reason with "Say why: this is the E&O record." Confirm with "Mark GRM-5512 lost? 2 renewal tasks close." Flash what changed, for example "Marked remarketing. Task 'Remarket …' added →". Apply the same reason rule to lost opportunities.
- **Verify:** A blank reason is refused, and the flash names the tasks affected.

### UX-050 — Stop dropping premiums with commas; show notes; record commission
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Producer recording a carrier's quote.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/sales/actions.ts:20,52` use a plain `Number()`. `sales/[id]/page.tsx:40-55` shows a Commission column with no input, and notes are saved but never displayed.
- **What the user experiences:** Typing "12,500" as the quote saves nothing, yet the flash says "Submission updated", and "Bind →" then opens with a blank premium. A note typed on a submission disappears from the page. Commission stays "—".
- **Why it matters:** Silent loss of a quote is worse than an error, and producers compare markets by premium and commission.
- **Recommendation:** Parse money the way `policies/actions.ts:17` does, and reject anything unreadable. Add a commission % input, and show notes under the carrier name.
- **Verify:** Enter "$12,500.00", and it shows and carries to Bind. A saved note stays visible.

### UX-051 — Keep a way back to the task on shortcut pages
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager interrupted midway through a task shortcut.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/certificates/new/page.tsx:38` (plain text "For task: …"), `policies/[id]/page.tsx:58` (nothing), `claims/new/page.tsx:22` (nothing).
- **What the user experiences:** After clicking "Endorse policy →", nothing says the page is tied to a task, and the crumbs lead to the client. To re-read the client's email, they must use the back button.
- **Why it matters:** The email and checklist are one click away but out of sight when entering the change.
- **Recommendation:** When `task` is present, show one bar above the form: "Working on: Add RAV4 to auto · Saving closes this task · ← Back to task".
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Clients / Brown Electric
  AFTER   ← Working on: Add RAV4 to auto · Saving updates this task  ◀
          Clients / Brown Electric
  ```
  Mockup: inline only
- **Verify:** From each shortcut, one click returns to the task.

### UX-052 — Keep the user's place while resolving statement lines
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Accounting manager reconciling a commission statement.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/accounting/actions.ts:95,150` and `commissions/[id]/page.tsx:55-60`.
- **What the user experiences:** Loading a file says "42 lines loaded and matched to policies", even when 7 didn't match. Each resolve reloads to the top, collapses the row and says only "Updated". The dollar difference isn't shown, so the user compares Paid and Expected by eye.
- **Why it matters:** "Matched" reads as verified, and the jump repeats for every exception on the statement.
- **Recommendation:** Flash "42 lines loaded: 35 matched, 4 with variance, 3 unmatched." Redirect resolved lines to `#line-{next}` with "Line accepted. 6 left." Add a "Diff" column, and name the amount on the button: "Accept carrier amount (−$14.20)". Also make the carrier a required choice with no preselection, so a file can't load against the first carrier in the list by default.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  ✔ Updated                        (page jumps to top)
          Paid $212.40  Expected $226.60  [Resolve]
  AFTER   ✔ Line accepted. 6 left.         (next exception in view) ◀
          Paid $212.40  Expected $226.60  Diff −$14.20              ◀
  ```
  Mockup: inline only
- **Verify:** Resolve three lines in a row without scrolling.

### UX-053 — Lay out the trust statement as arithmetic
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Accounting manager; principal checking the trust position.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/accounting/trust/page.tsx:29-30`.
- **What the user experiences:** Seven figures sit in a two-column label grid, with the excess at the end and a "not counted" figure among them. The user must work out which lines add up to what.
- **Why it matters:** This statement is the proof the books balance, so it should read as a calculation.
- **Recommendation:** Render aligned rows: trust cash, less each obligation, a total, then excess. Put "Not yet collected" below the line as a memo.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  TRUST CASH $84,210.00    OWED TO CARRIERS… $61,002.11
          OWED TO STATES $812.44   CLIENT REFUNDS $214.00 …
  AFTER   Trust cash                         $84,210.00       ◀
          less Carriers and wholesalers     −$61,002.11       ◀
          less States (surplus lines tax)      −$812.44       ◀
          less Client refunds                  −$214.00       ◀
          Excess available to sweep          $22,181.45       ◀
  ```
  Mockup: inline only
- **Verify:** The rows add to the excess on the page and in the sweep box.

### UX-054 — Connect endorsement, invoice and receipt
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** M
- **Who / when:** CSR answering "what did my check pay?"; account manager billing an endorsement.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/policies/actions.ts:87` (flash names no invoice), `policies/[id]/page.tsx:145-154` (no invoice link), `clients/[id]/page.tsx:376-390` (no applied-to detail; invoice numbers aren't links; PDF is the only document action).
- **What the user experiences:** An issued agency-bill endorsement flashes "Endorsement issued". The user isn't told an invoice exists, its number, or that someone must send it. On the Billing tab, a receipt doesn't show which invoices it paid.
- **Why it matters:** Billing questions need a trace from the change through to the payment, and an invoice nobody knows about doesn't get sent.
- **Recommendation:**
  - Flash "Endorsement issued. Invoice INV-26-0433 for $412.00 created. [Open PDF]".
  - Show the invoice beside its transaction.
  - On the Billing tab, list "Paid by RCT-26-0881, Oct 12" under each invoice and "Applied to …" under each receipt.
  - Add "Email invoice" where SMTP is on, or "Open PDF to attach" where it is off.
- **Verify:** From a policy transaction, reach its invoice and the receipt that paid it.

### UX-055 — Show term and status in the claim's policy list
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager recording a loss.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/claims/new/page.tsx:18,25,29`.
- **What the user experiences:** The list includes expired and cancelled terms, labelled only "GRM-GL-5512-02 · General liability · Granite Ridge". Consecutive terms look almost identical, so the date of loss can't be matched to the right one.
- **Why it matters:** A claim on the wrong term goes to the wrong record, and possibly the wrong carrier.
- **Recommendation:** Label options "… · Jun 8 2026–Jun 8 2027 · in force". Flag any picked term whose dates exclude the date of loss: "This term doesn't cover Nov 2, 2026."
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  GRM-GL-5512-02 · General liability · Granite Ridge
  AFTER   GRM-GL-5512-02 · GL · Jun 8 2026–Jun 8 2027 · in force  ◀
  ```
  Mockup: inline only
- **Verify:** A date of loss outside the chosen term shows a warning.

### UX-056 — Update the checklist when a task's type changes
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager correcting a misread email in triage.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/inbox/actions.ts:43` updates code, priority and subject only. `lib/work.ts:44` sets the checklist only at creation.
- **What the user experiences:** After retyping a task from a general inquiry to "Certificate request", the shortcut changes but the checklist still shows the old type's steps, and the due date keeps the old turnaround. The flash says only "Task type updated".
- **Why it matters:** The checklist then steers the user through the wrong job.
- **Recommendation:** Replace the checklist if nothing is ticked, otherwise append the new steps, and re-derive the due date unless a person set it. Flash "Now a Certificate request, due Nov 4. Task owner: Marisol Rivera."
- **Verify:** Retype a task, and its checklist matches the new type.

### UX-057 — Don't call it "Send reply" when nothing is sent
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Account manager replying while outbound email isn't connected.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/inbox/[id]/page.tsx:54`, `inbox/actions.ts:101-105`.
- **What the user experiences:** The button reads "Send reply". Afterwards a flash says it was logged, but the task note reads "Reply to …" with an "email" pill, and the Replies tab lists it like a real message. Anyone checking later would believe the client got it.
- **Why it matters:** This is the same false record UX-002 fixed for certificates.
- **Recommendation:** With SMTP off, label the button "Log reply (not sent)", show "Copy text to send from Outlook", store the note as "Not sent: reply drafted for …", and mark it in the Replies tab.
- **Verify:** With SMTP unset, no record implies the client received a reply.

### UX-058 — Mark required fields
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Everyone using a form, especially on rarely used pages.
- **Where:** `web/src/components/ui.tsx:162` has no required state, so none of the forms mark them.
- **What the user experiences:** Required and optional fields look alike until the browser stops the save at the first empty one.
- **Why it matters:** A marker before typing saves a failed submit on long forms such as New policy and New client.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `required` prop to `Field` that renders a small "Required" tag beside the label. Note once at the top of long forms, for example "Everything else is optional".
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  Carrier [Choose… ▾]    Effective date [..]
  AFTER   Carrier · Required [Choose… ▾]  Effective date · Required [..] ◀
  ```
  Mockup: inline only
- **Verify:** Each `required` input shows the marker.

### UX-059 — Bring the queue up on a phone and mark the current page
- **Status:** New
- **Effort:** S
- **Who / when:** Producer or account manager on a phone between client visits.
- **Where:** `web/src/app/(app)/page.tsx:100` (six tiles in two columns), `components/shell.tsx:52-54` (no active marker, `text-xs` links), `components/ui.tsx:12` (`btnSm` at `py-1`), `components/tasks.tsx:39`. Judged from classes only.
- **What the user experiences:** Three rows of tiles sit between the header and the queue. The top nav doesn't show the current page. "✓ Done" and "⏱ Later" are small targets sharing a row with a wrapping subject.
- **Why it matters:** The queue is the point of the screen, and small targets next to a one-tap completion invite slips.
- **Recommendation:** Below `sm`, show only Overdue, Due today and Emails as a compact strip. Add active styling and `aria-current` to `MobileNav`. Move quick actions onto their own line, with a minimum height of 40px.
- **Before / after:**
  ```
  BEFORE  [Overdue][Due today] / [Emails][Chase] / [Renewals][Done]
          Priority queue …
  AFTER   Overdue 4 · Today 7 · Email 3                      ◀
          Priority queue …
          [✓ Done]  [⏱ Later]    (40px, own row)             ◀
  ```
  Mockup: inline only
- **Verify:** At 375px, the first task is visible without scrolling and the nav shows the current page.

## P4 Polish

**UX-024 — Format the remaining dates one way.** (Improved, first seen 2026-11-01.) Waiting and snooze text is fixed. ISO dates remain in the non-pay panel and pending banner (`policies/[id]/page.tsx:77,131`), the policy header and every Term column, certificate terms and "Earliest expiration", and automation task subjects (`lib/automation.ts:33`). Use `whenDate` in running text.

**UX-060 — Make the My Day badge match the header count.** (New.) The sidebar counts tasks due by today (`layout.tsx:20-21`). "N tasks need you today" also counts urgent tasks due later (`priority.ts:115`), and the daily non-pay check creates exactly those. Use the same rule for both.

**UX-061 — Say "today", not "0d" or "-5d".** (New.) The queue chips are fixed, but the raw form remains on the renewals board (`renewals/page.tsx:90`), the policy list (`policies/page.tsx:63`), the client overview, which can show a negative (`clients/[id]/page.tsx:105`), and the header's "(0 days left)". Use `daysLeft`, and "expired" for negatives.

**UX-062 — Use one word per thing.** (New.) Examples:
- "Next week" vs "1 week" for the same snooze (`tasks.tsx:48`, `tasks/[id]/page.tsx:181`).
- "Coming later" and "Needs setup" on controls vs "Not in MVP" and "Pending dependency" on the Roadmap they link to (`admin/roadmap/page.tsx:12`).
- "statement … loaded by ai" (`commissions/[id]/page.tsx:41`).
- A bare "Create" on the opportunity form.
- The Book report's plain "Download CSV" link vs the button elsewhere.

**UX-063 — Hide dead ends; guard the `n` shortcut.** (New.) A CSR's Reports page holds only a sentence saying reports are for others, plus two "Coming later" tags; hide the nav item for roles with no reports. Admin cards a non-admin can't open are dimmed but still link to a refusal; remove them. Pressing `n` outside a field jumps to the next task and discards any half-filled form (`shell.tsx:88`), and the README says `n` creates a task. Skip the shortcut on pages with a form, and correct the README.

## What works well
- **Non-pay panel.** `policies/[id]/page.tsx:75-100` leads with the notice date, puts "Payment confirmed: reinstate" first, and opens "Carrier cancelled it" only from the cancel date. Don't turn it back into a generic form.
- **Money confirmations.** `lib/receipt-confirm.ts` and `components/money-confirm.tsx` word the receipt dialog from the actual form: amount, check number, invoices reached and any credit. Other trust actions name payee and amount too.
- **Statement readiness.** `commissions/[id]/page.tsx:74-79` shows a ✔/✖ checklist and a disabled button that says what's left ("Resolve 7 lines to post").
- **Dead certificates look dead.** A PDF watermark, a replacement banner and "Open current certificate →" work together (`pdf.ts:70`, `certificates/[id]/page.tsx:43-46`). The delivery wording is now honest about what was sent.
- **Forms that come back as typed.** The `rejected()` and `fieldsOf()` pattern (`lib/form-state.ts`) keeps values and task links, and the duplicate-client banner offers "Open existing" and "Create anyway".
- **The picker's refusal.** `client-picker.tsx` won't save half-typed text and won't save a client other than the one shown. Keep that rule while removing the extra Load step (UX-037).

## Declined
None.

## Coverage notes
- **App status:** Not running. `/api/live` returned nothing and the home page didn't contain "siryous AMS", so no pages were fetched. Everything was judged from source. Rendered layout, phone behaviour, browser validation bubbles and PDFs were not seen.
- **Read in full:** shell, My Day, tasks, inbox, clients, policies, renewals, sales, certificates, claims, accounting, reports, the admin pages other than App Tests, sign-in, quote, search, shared components, `actions.ts` files, `lib/priority.ts`, `lib/work.ts`, `lib/certificates.ts`, `lib/receipt-confirm.ts` and `lib/pdf.ts`.
- **Read in part:** `lib/policies.ts`, `lib/automation.ts`, `lib/accounting.ts`, `lib/email/ingest.ts`, `lib/format.ts` and `lib/roadmap.ts`, where they reach the UI.
- **Not reviewed:** `components/charts.tsx`, `components/markdown.tsx`, CSV exports, `api/*`, and the `/admin/app-tests` source and page.
- **Guard limits:** Two read-only commands were refused by the review guard and rerun in a permitted form. The App Tests page was not fetched.
- **Scope:** "Coming later" and "Needs setup" controls were judged only on how clearly they are tagged.
- **Mockups:** Six new mockups this run. Existing mockups for UX-006 and UX-037 remain usable; the UX-037 mockup shows the right direction, but its "before" predates the blocking behaviour.
